items.title: New optogenetic tool inhibits activity in neurons and heart muscle cells
paras: Researchers from Ruhr University Bochum have partnered with colleagues in Göttingen, Berlin, Paris and Essen to develop new optogenetic tools that can selectively inhibit cellular activity through light. These tools could help investigate diseases in which the balance between excitation and inhibition is disrupted, such as cardiac arrhythmias.

paras: India swung for the moon with Chandrayaan-1, its first deep space mission. Click for next article Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter On Oct.

21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL.

items.title: Anderson, 44, not offered new Lancashire contract
paras: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, James Anderson is England's all-time leading Test wicket-taker with 704 dismissals Cricket Correspondent Published 21 October 2026, 16:11 BST Updated 8 hours ago James Anderson's legendary career could be over after Lancashire opted against offering England's all-time leading wicket-taker a new contract.

Anderson, 44, chose to continue playing with Lancashire after England forced him into international retirement in 2024. He captained Lancashire in the County Championship last season but the Red Rose endured a poor campaign, finishing next to bottom of Division Two. Now, as first reported by the Times, Anderson will not be given the opportunity to play at Old Trafford in 2027 - the summer when he will turn 45.

items.title: Mine on tropical island plans to pump pit water into ocean
paras: The Groote Archipelago is home to several Anindilyakwa communities and the GEMCO manganese mine. South32 wants to build pumps and pipelines on Groote Eylandt to take up to 80 gigalitres of water per year from the mining pit to the ocean.

The plan has the support of traditional owners and environmental approval, and comes as the company tries to address massive water management costs. Further consultation is required as the infrastructure would be partially built on Aboriginal-owned land. South32 plans to spend $100 million to pump water from its Northern Territory manganese mine into the ocean as it battles to keep the site open.

items.title: Calls for transparency as pressure builds on regional SA health system
paras: SASMOA says its members reported having 30 patients and 12 treatment areas at Mount Gambier hospital. ( ABC South East SA: Bec Whetham ) The SA Salaried Medical Officers Association says more data should be made available on the pressure regional emergency departments are under.

The union's members reported severe overcapacity in Mount Gambier's ED last Wednesday. Health Minister Blair Boyer says he will consider making more data available. There are concerns a lack of data on regional hospital demand is obscuring the strain the system is under, with reports an SA emergency department had twice as many patients as it did treatment spaces.

items.title: Author Helen Fielding launches award to find the next Bridget Jones's Diary
paras: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Bridget Jones author Helen Fielding (right) alongside film star Renée Zellweger Bridget Jones author Helen Fielding has launched a new prize aimed at discovering funny diary writers from the north of England, saying opportunities across the UK are "very uneven".

West Yorkshire-born Fielding, who penned Bridget's famous diary as well co-writing the film adaptations, has set up the Bridget Jones Prize , external with charity New Writing North. The award will go to the person who submits the funniest 1,000-word piece of first-person writing.

items.title: McCartney and Starr back new Beatles attraction
paras: Image source, Apple Corps Ltd Image caption, Artist's impression of plans for a Yellow Submarine experience at St John's Beacon Sir Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr have backed plans for a major new Beatles visitor attraction in Liverpool.

The development will see The Beatles Story move from Albert Dock to the former St John's Market site, alongside a new Yellow Submarine experience at St John's Beacon. McCartney said he "can't wait" for people to be able to "step into our story", while Starr said: "Liverpool was, and still is, Music City".
